title: People Ops — Hiring, Onboarding, Performance & Manager Playbook
author: Asha Patel
body:
Summary

This playbook documents Redwood Inference’s standard processes for hiring, employee onboarding, performance and feedback cycles, and manager responsibilities. It is intended for hiring managers, interviewers, people-ops partners, and new managers. Follow the steps and templates below to ensure a consistent, inclusive, and legally compliant employee lifecycle.

Scope

- Applies to all full-time employees (FTEs), contractors (with recruiting guidance), and interns unless an exception is documented with People Ops.
- Covers: requisition approval, sourcing, interview loop design, debriefs and scorecards, offer process, background checks, first-90-day onboarding, 30/60/90 plans, ongoing feedback cadence, performance review schedule, calibration, promotions, and off-boarding basics.

Guiding principles

1. Candidate experience: timely communication, clear expectations, and constructive feedback. Target: first recruiter reach-out within 48 business hours.
2. Consistency: use standardized scorecards and role-specific rubrics to reduce bias.
3. Speed + quality: target time-to-offer median 35 calendar days for engineering roles.
4. Manager enablement: provide playbooks, templates, and People Ops partnership for compliance and difficult cases.

Hiring process (high level)

1) Requisition and hiring plan
   - Manager creates a requisition in Workday (or internal ATS) with role summary, band/level, and justification.
   - Required approvals: Manager -> Director -> Finance (headcount) -> People Ops.
   - Include posting language, must-have/soft-preferences, and expected interviewers.

2) Sourcing and screening
   - Recruiter runs sourcing plan (inbound, referrals, external pipelines).
   - Initial phone screen (30m) covers: role fit, salary expectations, work authorization, and basic technical/behavioral fit.
   - Screen outcomes: advance to loop | hold | decline.

3) Interview loop design
   - Standard loop for IC engineering roles (example):
     a) Technical take-home or screening challenge (optional for senior roles)
     b) Technical deep-dive (60m) – system design or architecture for senior, coding interview for ICs
     c) Collaboration & exec presence (45m) – cross-functional/communication
     d) Culture & leadership (30m) – values and behavioral fit
     e) Final hiring manager debrief
   - Use published role rubric for scoring (see "Interview scorecard template" below).

4) Debrief and decision
   - Debrief within 48 hours of last interview. Recruiter schedules debrief and ensures scorecards completed.
   - Decision: Strong Yes | Yes with concerns | No, with written rationale required for No.
   - For split votes, hiring manager & recruiter consult People Ops for calibration.

5) Offer, negotiation, and close
   - Offer letter drafted by Recruiter with compensation, equity (if applicable), benefits link, start date, and relocation/visa notes.
   - Regulatory: all offers require final sign-off by People Ops and Finance for banding compliance.
   - Target offer window: extend verbal offer within 2 business days after decision.

6) Pre-hire checks
   - Contingent on offer acceptance: background check, reference checks (role-dependent), and work authorization verification.
   - Any flagged result escalates to People Ops and Legal.

Interview scorecard template (example)

- Score scale: 1 (does not meet) | 2 (below) | 3 (meets) | 4 (exceeds) | 5 (exceptional)
- Sections (each a single numeric score + short commentary):
  - Technical competence
  - Problem solving & design
  - Communication and collaboration
  - Product/contextual sense
  - Culture / company values alignment
  - Role-specific competency (e.g., serving runtime, infra, SRE)

Notes to interviewers:
- Provide concrete examples; avoid vague phrases.
- Focus feedback on behaviors, not personality.
- Flag potential legal concerns to People Ops immediately (e.g., inappropriate questions).

Inclusive hiring checklists

- At least one diverse slate or documented outreach effort before on-site for senior roles.
- Use structured interview questions.
- Inclusive language in job postings (guidance available in recruiting toolkit).

Onboarding (first 90 days)

Principles: fast ramp, clear expectations, early connection to team and product, and compliance completion.

Day 0–1 (pre-start & first day)
- People Ops sends welcome packet with offer letter, benefits enrollment links, and first-day schedule.
- IT provisions laptop, credentials, and access to Slack, Google Workspace, GitHub, internal docs, and Redwood Console demo account where applicable.
- Manager schedules 1:1 (30m) for first day, assigns buddy, and shares 30/60/90 plan template.
- New hire completes payroll, tax forms, I-9 (or local equivalent), and mandatory security & compliance training within 3 business days.

Week 1
- Meet the team: schedule introductions with cross-functional partners (Product, SRE, Research).
- Product walkthrough and architecture overview (45–60m).
- Role-specific onboarding: sandbox tasks, access to staging environments, and small first-ticket to complete.
- Manager and buddy establish learning goals and checkpoints.

First 30 days (ramp and learning)
- Complete required reading list: product docs, runtime architecture, operational runbooks.
- Deliverable: complete onboarding task and demo to manager.
- Weekly 1:1s, and end-of-month check-in with People Ops for administrative confirmation.

30–90 days (impact and autonomy)
- Manager reviews growth plan and checkpoints at 30, 60, 90 days.
- Candidate ramp goal: independently take ownership of a small project or feature and demonstrate cross-team collaboration.

Onboarding checklist (table)

| Item | Owner | Target completion | Notes |
|------|-------|-------------------|-------|
| Offer acceptance & paperwork | People Ops | Day 0 | Benefits packet sent |
| Laptop & accounts provisioned | IT | Day 0 | Access to required repos |
| Security training | New hire | Day 3 | Phishing awareness, SSO setup |
| Buddy assigned | Manager | Day 0 | Peer mentor for first 90 days |
| First ticket assigned | Manager | Week 1 | Clear success criteria |

Performance & feedback cycle

Cadence
- Ongoing: continuous feedback (documented in manager notes and Slack threads).
- Quarterly: goal check-ins and 1:1 performance conversations.
- Semi-annual/annual: formal performance reviews and calibration.
- Promotion cycles: scheduled quarterly calibration meetings; promotions decisions documented with justification and data.

Performance review timeline (example)
- Goal-setting window: first two weeks of fiscal quarter.
- Midpoint check-in: end of quarter midpoint.
- Formal review window: Q4 annual review (dates published the start of the fiscal year).

Manager checklist for reviews
1. Ensure goals are specific, measurable and recorded in the goal tracker (link in templates).
2. Collect evidence: tickets, PRs, customer feedback, on-call incident responses.
3. Provide balanced narrative (strengths, growth areas, proposed next band/level if applicable).
4. Schedule calibration session with peers and People Ops.
5. Communicate outcome and next steps to the employee with an actionable development plan.

Constructive feedback best practices
- Use Situation-Behavior-Impact (SBI) framework.
- Give feedback frequently and in private for developmental topics.
- Document conversations and follow-up actions.

Promotion & leveling guidance
- Promotion criteria include demonstrated scope increase, consistent delivery above level, and leadership/mentorship evidence.
- Manager prepares a promotion packet: current role summary, evidence bullets, peer feedback, and proposed new level.
- Packet reviewed by calibration panel and People Ops for equity and consistency.

Manager responsibilities (short guide)

- Hiring: define role, interviewers, and assess candidates with the standardized rubric.
- Onboarding: set clear 30/60/90 goals, schedule regular 1:1s, assign a buddy, and ensure training completion.
- Performance: provide continuous feedback, run formal reviews, and advocate for team members in calibration.
- Development: support career conversations, create development plans, and allocate stretch projects.
- Compliance & safety: ensure employees complete mandatory trainings and follow security policies.

Escalation paths
- People Ops: people-ops@redwood-inference.com — for policy exceptions, compensation questions, and compliance issues.
- Legal: legal@redwood-inference.com — for contract/visa/immigration escalations.
- Finance: payroll@redwood-inference.com — for payroll and benefits discrepancies.
- Recruiting lead: diego.martinez@redwood-inference.com — for sourcing and high-priority roles.

Templates & artifacts (links and snippets)

- 30/60/90 plan template (copyable):
  - 30 days: learn, small-ticket completion, meet stakeholders
  - 60 days: take ownership of feature, contribute to design reviews
  - 90 days: deliver measurable impact, own cross-cutting task

- Interview scorecard (see earlier)
- Offer letter checklist: comp, equity, start date, remote location policy, relocation/visa notes, probation period where applicable.
- Sample onboarding schedule (first week): Day 1 admin + team intro; Day 2 product deep-dive; Day 3 hands-on pairing; Day 4 cross-team sync; Day 5 demo + retro.

Common scenarios and guidance

- Counteroffers: document candidate justification; discuss retention vs. new hire fit with People Ops.
- Late starts: update matter in ATS, adjust onboarding schedule, notify IT for delayed provisioning.
- Failed background check: People Ops performs case review and consults Legal.
- Rehire candidates: follow rehire policy and ensure eligibility review in People Ops.

Metrics and KPIs People Ops tracks
- Time-to-fill (median days to offer) — target 35 days (engineering)
- Offer acceptance rate — target >= 75%
- New hire 90-day retention — target >= 90%
- Hiring source conversion rates (referrals, inbound, agency)
- Manager satisfaction with candidates (post-hire survey)

Appendix: quick checklists

Manager pre-hire checklist
- Requisition submitted and approved
- Interviewers scheduled and scorecards created
- Job posting reviewed for inclusive language
- Compensation band / target discussed with Finance

New hire first week checklist
- Access: Slack, GitHub, CI/CD, internal docs
- Meetings: team intro, product overview, 1:1 scheduled
- Admin: payroll, benefits enrollment, security training
